picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
picks.rationale: This is the reason the case was sent, and the upside is a durable graft-versus-leukemia remission with almost no collateral: Krakow 2024 saw CR achieved or maintained in 4 of 9 post-HCT relapses, zero DLTs, and no CRS or ICANS, with one patient past two years. HA-1 sits only on blood-lineage cells, so the killing stays in the compartment we want it. The catch is real and I will not bury it: eligibility gates on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and none of that is typed yet, so backing this pick is a bet that the pending typing comes back in our favor. n=9 is a feasibility cohort, not an efficacy result.
primary_concerns: Gated on unresolved HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1(H) genotyping of both patient and sibling donor; the whole pathway collapses if either misses
n=9 feasibility cohort with no efficacy powering
Needs cytoreduction and a second-transplant platform in place first; 85% blast burden may outpace TCR-T kinetics

picks.rationale: For an 85%-blast marrow with extramedullary disease, the honest problem is getting this patient to a second transplant alive and deep enough for it to hold, and SIERRA is the one randomized signal that speaks to exactly that: durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care. It carries active disease into allo-HCT instead of demanding a remission the chemotherapy can no longer deliver, which is the crux of a curative plan here. The soft spot: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility is unproven, and the go-forward NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting. ITT OS was flat, but that reflects 52% crossover to the radioconjugate, not failed conditioning.
primary_concerns: Prior allo-HCT eligibility for CD45 radioimmunotherapy is unestablished; SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients
Go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting
Second-transplant treatment-related mortality; fitness and organ-function workup still open

picks.rationale: CD123 is confirmed on the blasts, and pivekimab is the CD123 ADC with real single-agent R/R AML numbers rather than cross-tumor read-across: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the RP2D. I want it as debulking ahead of the cellular and transplant consolidation, not as a destination in itself. Preclinically the mono-alkylator payload kills at low-picomolar potency below the dose that touches normal progenitors (Kovtun 2018), so the therapeutic window is plausible if the pending quantitative CD123 density holds up. Two flags I will name: response depth is modest, and the veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses matters with a transplant coming.
primary_concerns: ORR 21% is modest; single agent unlikely to clear an 85% blast burden on its own
Veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses is a concern ahead of HCT2
Quantitative CD123 antigen density that predicts ADC benefit is still pending

picks.rationale: Here is the mechanistic bet I will make in the open: TP53-aberrant AML runs an inflamed, IFN-gamma-high marrow, and on the flotetuzumab trial 7 of 15 TP53-abnormal R/R patients dropped under 5% blasts, with ORR 30% in the primary-refractory/early-relapse group. If this patient's TP53 status confirms, that biology is a live reason to expect CD123xCD3 redirection to bite harder here than the pooled numbers imply. The hard truth: MacroGenics deprioritized the program, so this is mechanism evidence and a case for chasing an open CD123xCD3 or dual CD33/CD123 construct, not an enrollable slot. CRS is the class risk and autologous T-cell fitness in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow is unknown.
primary_concerns: Program discontinued; no open enrollment route for flotetuzumab itself
The TP53-inflamed-marrow rationale hinges on the unconfirmed TP53 status resolving aberrant
CRS/infusion reactions and uncertain T-cell fitness after prior transplant and FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure

notes: Curative-intent package sequenced as one plan rather than four independent bets: CD123-directed debulking (pivekimab, or the TP53-inflamed-marrow case for a CD123xCD3 construct) to knock down the 85% blast load, Iomab-B conditioning to carry active disease into HCT2, then HA-1 TCR-T as post-transplant graft-versus-leukemia consolidation. HLA-A*02:01 typing plus HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor is the master switch for rank 1 and the WT1/PRAME fallbacks (A*24:02 WT1-siTCR if A*02:01-negative); every HLA-restricted lever is stranded until that comes back. Left the Y220C-selective rezatapopt off my ranked picks because it has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy yet and is double-gated on confirming TP53 aberrant and specifically Y220C, but if that variant confirms it jumps up fast given the strong Carter 2025 AML preclinical signal.

picks.rationale: The thing I keep coming back to is that SIERRA is the only randomized phase 3 in this whole dossier that speaks to the actual problem, getting an 85%-blast marrow through to a transplant. It gave durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, and the toxicity is what earns it my rank 1: grade 3+ treatment-related AEs ran 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care, so as conditioning the radioconjugate adds essentially no incremental grade 3+ burden. This is published 2025 randomized data with per-term AEs posted on the NCT02665065 tab, not a single-arm signal I have to take on trust. My hesitation is honest: SIERRA enrolled patients going to a first transplant, so second-transplant TRM and prior-HCT eligibility are unproven, and this patient has no organ-function labs on file yet.
primary_concerns: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients; second-transplant TRM and prior-HCT eligibility are not established
No numeric organ-function labs on file; radioimmunotherapy conditioning ahead of HCT2 needs cardiac, renal, and hepatic clearance first
Not FDA-approved; the go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting

picks.rationale: This is the CD33 handle with the longest safety record I have to work with: an FDA-approved ADC with roughly 25 years of post-marketing data and a worked-out hepatic and veno-occlusive-disease monitoring algorithm, and the fractionated 3 mg/m2 schedule cut early deaths at equal efficacy in the Hills IPD meta-analysis. What stops me ranking it higher is that same tier-1a meta-analysis: across 3325 patients the adverse-cytogenetics subgroup got OR 0.99 for 5-year OS (95% CI 0.83-1.18), meaning no benefit, and this patient's complex TP53-aberrant karyotype sits squarely in that subgroup. The single-agent relapse data are modest too, 30% CR/CRp (Sievers 2001), and that was a cleaner first-relapse population than this FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory one with extramedullary disease. The grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia rate of 23% is also exactly the wrong toxicity to invite ahead of a second transplant.
primary_concerns: Tier-1a Hills meta shows no OS benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18), the patient's exact subgroup
Hepatic and VOD risk (grade 3+ hyperbilirubinemia 23%) compounds with a planned HCT2
Single-agent CR/CRp 30% came from first relapse, not this refractory extramedullary state

picks.rationale: Among the CD123 options this is the only FDA-approved agent, about 8 years of post-marketing use with a defined capillary-leak management algorithm covering albumin thresholds, daily weights, blood-pressure monitoring, and dose holds, which is why I take it over pivekimab or the discontinued flotetuzumab. But the approval is in BPDCN, not AML, so the 72% first-line CR (21/29, Pemmaraju 2019) is cross-tumor read-across and does not transfer cleanly to an 85%-blast AML marrow. Capillary leak syndrome carries a boxed warning and showed up in 19% with a death in each dose subgroup, and with no organ-function labs on file I will not commit to it before the fitness and cardiac workup lands. I rank it, but low, and behind a clear read on this patient's albumin and cardiac reserve.
primary_concerns: FDA approval is in BPDCN; AML use is off-label cross-tumor read-across
Capillary leak syndrome (19%, one death per dose subgroup) with undocumented organ function
Needs baseline albumin and cardiac/hepatic workup before it is safe to start

notes: toxicity_vetoes is empty, so I issue no round-1 veto, but the place I will be watching in round 2 is any CD33/CD123 ADC or immunotoxin proposed ahead of HCT2 without a documented organ-function clearance: veno-occlusive disease (gemtuzumab, pivekimab) and capillary leak (tagraxofusp) are the toxicities I would gate on albumin, hepatic, and cardiac baselines. I deliberately left the HLA-restricted cellular therapies off my ranked picks even though they are the stated reason for the case. HA-1 TCR-T (Krakow 2024, n=9), the WT1 TCR products, and multiantigen TAA-T are all phase-1/feasibility with no post-marketing safety follow-up and long-tail toxicity I cannot characterize, and every one is gated on HLA typing that is not back yet. I am not vetoing them: HA-1 read clean, 0 CRS and 0 ICANS across 9 patients, which is the opposite of what I worry about. If the typing confirms eligibility they belong in the curative plan as post-HCT2 consolidation, but I will not rank feasibility-grade evidence above a randomized phase 3 and an FDA-approved ADC. Eprenetapopt stays off too: it is a pan-p53 reactivator, not Y220C-selective, and its randomized phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed.

picks.rationale: SIERRA is the one randomized phase 3 in this dossier that points toward benefit, and its registered primary endpoint cleared conventional alpha: durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, p<0.0001. Two things hold me at moderate rather than high. The endpoint is a surrogate, durable CR at 180 days rather than survival, and ITT OS was flat at HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41), which the 52% crossover to the radioconjugate explains but does not undo. And SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so reading it onto a prior-HCT relapse is indirect evidence rather than tested ground; RoB2 for the trial is Some concerns, driven by open-label conduct, though a durable-CR endpoint is objective enough to blunt detection bias.
primary_concerns: RoB2 domain 4 (outcome measurement): open-label conduct, partly offset because durable CR >=180d is an objective endpoint
Primary endpoint is a surrogate (durable CR), not OS; ITT OS null at HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41)
RoB2 domain 2 (deviations from intended intervention): 52% crossover to the radioconjugate confounds the OS comparison
Applicability / indirectness: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility is untested

picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
picks.rationale: This is the stated reason the case was sent, so I will rank it, but I will not dress up n=9 as efficacy evidence. Krakow 2024 is a single-arm feasibility cohort with no comparator and no pre-specified efficacy endpoint, so the 4-of-9 CR cannot be pulled apart from the lymphodepletion effect or the natural clonal course. What it does show, backed by the Dossa 2018 construct work, is a clean safety read: zero DLTs, zero CRS, zero ICANS across 9 patients. Eligibility is still unconfirmed, since HLA-A*02:01 and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch are both pending, so any support here stays conditional on the typing coming back in favor.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding domain: single-arm with no comparator, so 4/9 CR cannot be separated from lymphodepletion or clonal course
n=9 feasibility cohort with no pre-specified efficacy endpoint and no efficacy powering
Eligibility unconfirmed: HLA-A*02:01 status and the HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch are both pending

notes: Two picks by design. The dossier holds exactly one randomized trial pointing toward benefit on a question that fits this patient (SIERRA), and I ranked it; I declined to rank the rest on evidence-quality grounds. Gemtuzumab actually carries the highest-tier data in the file, ALFA-0701 (RoB2:Low, pmid 22482940) and the Hills IPD meta-analysis (tier 1a, pmid 25008258), but both are front-line, and the pre-specified adverse-cytogenetics stratum is null at OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.83-1.18). Read rigorously, the strongest evidence in the dossier argues against use in this complex-karyotype R/R patient, not for it. Pivekimab and tagraxofusp are single-arm with response-rate surrogates (pivekimab ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; tagraxofusp sits in BPDCN, cross-tumor read-across). Flotetuzumab's TP53 signal (7/15 reaching under 5% blasts) is an unadjusted post-hoc subgroup from a correlative study on a program that has since been deprioritized. Eprenetapopt is the replication-failure exhibit: single-arm ORR 64-71%, then a randomized phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS that missed its primary endpoint, so I would not build on it. Rezatapopt has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy at all (logged considered_excluded) and is double-gated on confirming TP53 aberration and specifically Y220C, so from where I sit it is preclinical-only.

picks.intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning + allo-HCT (HCT2 platform)
picks.rationale: For a fit patient relapsing after allo-HCT with curative intent, the prevailing consensus points at a second allograft: ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022) and NCCN AML v3.2026 both keep second allo-HCT and clinical-trial enrollment in play for relapsed disease, and that is where the curative goal actually lives. Iomab-B is the conditioning that carries an 85%-blast marrow into that transplant, and it enters through NCCN's category-2A clinical-trial-preferred route rather than as a categorized drug, backed by SIERRA, the one randomized phase 3 in this dossier (durable CR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001). I rank it first because it fits the stated curative intent under a route NCCN, ELN, and ASH converge on, not because the agent itself carries a label. The honest gap: ELN's second-transplant consensus assumes a transplant-fit patient, and this one has no cardiac or organ-function workup on file yet.
primary_concerns: ELN 2022's second-transplant consensus assumes a transplant-fit patient; no documented cardiac, renal, or hepatic workup yet, so the guideline-endorsed population is not established

Iomab-B carries no NCCN drug-level category; it is guideline-aligned only through the clinical-trial-enrollment principle, and SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility sits outside the studied population
Go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting

picks.rationale: This is the one agent in the dossier that is both FDA-approved and guideline-listed against a target the patient actually carries: NCCN AML v3.2026 keeps gemtuzumab ozogamicin as a category-2A option for relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML, and the blasts are CD33-positive by flow. What holds it at rank 2 rather than 1 is that the patient sits in the wrong subgroup, since the tier-1a Hills IPD meta-analysis found no survival signal in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18), which is exactly this complex, TP53-aberrant karyotype. Single-agent depth in relapse was modest to begin with (30% CR/CRp, Sievers 2001) and came from a cleaner first-relapse population than this FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory state with extramedullary disease. The hepatic and veno-occlusive-disease risk is also the wrong toxicity to invite right before a planned second transplant.
primary_concerns: Guideline benefit does not reach this patient's stratum: Hills tier-1a meta null in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18), the exact complex/TP53-aberrant subgroup
NCCN category 2A covers R/R CD33+ AML broadly; the on-label monotherapy data (30% CR/CRp) came from first relapse, not this refractory extramedullary presentation
Hepatic / VOD risk compounds with the planned HCT2

picks.intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
picks.rationale: HLA-restricted cellular therapy is the reason the case was sent, and the guidelines give it a home, but only at the level of the route rather than the product. NCCN AML v3.2026 marks clinical-trial enrollment as the category-2A preferred path for relapsed/refractory disease, and ELN 2022 keeps adoptive cellular approaches open for post-transplant relapse, so HA-1 TCR-T is guideline-aligned as a trial (NCT03326921; commercial TSC-100 on NCT05473910). What it does not have is a drug-level category or any efficacy powering, since Krakow 2024 is an n=9 feasibility cohort (4 of 9 in CR, zero CRS/ICANS). And the whole lever is gated on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, none of which is typed yet.
primary_concerns: Guideline support is for trial enrollment as a category, not for this specific product; no NCCN drug-level category and no efficacy-powered data (n=9 feasibility)
Eligibility population unconfirmed: HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative genotyping of patient and sibling donor are all pending
ELN 2022 offers no consensus sequencing of DLI vs second transplant vs cellular therapy for post-HCT relapse, so this sits in a genuinely under-specified guideline zone

notes: Ranked to guideline fit: the curative backbone (second allo-HCT, endorsed by ELN 2022 Dohner Blood 2022 and NCCN AML v3.2026) at rank 1 via Iomab-B conditioning, the sole FDA-approved/NCCN-listed on-target agent (gemtuzumab, NCCN AML v3.2026 category 2A for R/R CD33+) at rank 2, and the stated-reason HLA-restricted cellular therapy at rank 3 through NCCN's category-2A clinical-trial-preferred principle. Left off-guideline options out of the ranked picks and flag them here: tagraxofusp is FDA-approved only in BPDCN, so AML use is off-label cross-tumor read-across (disfavored); pivekimab, flotetuzumab, and vibecotamab are investigational or discontinued CD123 constructs with no guideline listing (trial-enrollment route only); on the TP53 axis, eprenetapopt is not guideline-endorsed and its randomized phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint, and rezatapopt has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy and is double-gated on confirming TP53 aberration and specifically Y220C. No veto: nothing in the dossier is guideline-contraindicated for this population; guideline-fit alone is not a safety issue. Master unknown across every ranked pick is fitness/organ-function, which the preferences flag as an open item and which the transplant-consensus population assumes is settled.

picks.rationale: Debulking bridge. The marrow is 85% blasts and refractory to FLAG-IDA/venetoclax, and neither the TCR-T nor the transplant bites on a marrow that full. CD123 is a user-named handle (positive by flow), pivekimab is the CD123 ADC with its own R/R AML numbers rather than borrowed ones (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; composite CR 17%), and it runs through a trial (NCT03386513), which prefers_trials favors. The efficacy-leaning weight supports using it to buy the deeper cytoreduction the curative plan needs. Two caveats: single-agent depth is modest, and the veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses matters with a transplant coming. Since toxicity_vetoes is empty, that VOD flag is a fitness judgment rather than a preference breach. Quantitative CD123 density is still pending.
primary_concerns: Satisfied: CD123 is a user-named handle, a trial route (prefers_trials), and the efficacy-leaning weight supports debulking.
In tension: single-agent depth is modest against an 85% blast load and unlikely to clear it alone.
The VOD signal ahead of HCT2 is a fitness consideration, not a preference veto (toxicity_vetoes is empty); quantitative CD123 antigen density is pending.

picks.rationale: This is here for one job: keep the HLA immunotherapy door open if A*02:01 types negative. The preferences call de-risking the HLA-restricted pathway the priority, and that means holding a fallback ready, not just the A*02:01 lever. WT1-siTCR is A*24:02-restricted, so an A*02:01-negative but A*24:02-positive patient still has an immunotherapy route rather than a dead end. The Tawara 2017 cohort is small (n=8) and early, with transient blast reductions and no normal-tissue toxicity, so I treat this as a bridge concept, not a proven salvage. It is the reason both HLA alleles should be pulled in parallel instead of A*02:01 alone.
primary_concerns: Satisfied: directly serves the stated priority of de-risking the HLA-restricted immunotherapy pathway by keeping a route open if A*02:01 is negative.
In tension: gated on A*24:02 typing, also unresolved, and only relevant if the A*02:01 axis is foreclosed.
Evidence is n=8 early-phase with transient responses; a fallback lever, not a primary efficacy bet.

notes: My ranking follows the user's stated lens rather than pure evidence tier. The preferences name HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason for the run and call de-risking that pathway the priority, so HA-1 TCR-T leads and the A*24:02 WT1-siTCR fallback is ranked to hold the door open if A*02:01 types negative. The master switch under all of it is the pending HLA-A*02:01 typing plus HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor; both alleles should be pulled in parallel. Iomab-B and pivekimab are the enabling platform and the debulking bridge that make the cellular consolidation deliverable against an 85%-blast marrow, consistent with the curative intent and the 0.75 efficacy-leaning weight. Two preference axes do no filtering work here: toxicity_vetoes is empty and modality_constraints is empty, so nothing was excluded on preference grounds, and HCT2, cellular therapy, and trial travel are all explicitly acceptable. The caveat I echo from the free_text: the 0.75 efficacy weight is provisional and should be revisited once ECOG/cardiac/organ-function and goals-of-care are documented, since every pick here assumes transplant-grade fitness that is not yet established. Fallbacks I did not rank but flag: the TAA-T multiantigen product (PRAME/WT1/Survivin, NCT02203903) leans less on a single HLA gate and is a recruiting post-HCT option, and CBX-250 (NCT06994676) is an off-the-shelf A*02:01 T-cell engager with no manufacturing lead time. Rezatapopt stays off my ranked list: it is double-gated on confirming TP53 aberration and specifically Y220C and has no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy yet, so it cannot carry a rank even though the user named the TP53 handle.
